value: The attacker used DVWA SQL injection with sqlmap to write temp PHP web shells via INTO OUTFILE, then executed them to issue commands and delete the shells.
evidence: Lines 7605-7608 and 7662-7664 in work/extracted/s50bb03/logs/access.log show sqlmap/1.0-dev-nongit-20150902 writing /tmpbiwuc.php and /tmpbrjvl.php with cmd=... and deleting them; full file hash can be checked on disk.

value: File /xampp/htdocs/DVWA/c99.php was present on disk and served to the attacker; it is a PHP web shell with system($_GET["cmd"]).
evidence: Open and inspect work/extracted/s50bb03/dvwa/xampp_htdocs_DVWA_c99.php; first lines are '<?php system($_GET["cmd"]); ?>', and Apache log line 7688 shows GET /dvwa/c99.php.

value: File /xampp/htdocs/DVWA/hackable/uploads/phpshell2.php was present on disk and contains a reverse shell that connects to 192.168.56.102:4545.
evidence: Inspect the extracted file; its first line hard-codes IP 192.168.56.102 and port 4545 and uses stream_socket_client/fsockopen/socket_create before eval($b).

value: A leftover copy of c99.php existed in %TEMP% as c99 (2).php, indicating the attacker's web shell was also staged outside the web root.
evidence: The extracted file work/extracted/s50bb03/temp/c99_(2).php is a copy of the c99 web shell; compare it to the web-root copy to see matching contents.

value: The host had XAMPP 5.6.11-1 and Microsoft Visual C++ 2008 Redistributable installed; XAMPP was installed via the Bitnami installer, not by the attacker based on the install registry values and dated XAMPP directory metadata.
evidence: HKLM\...\Uninstall\xampp reports DisplayName XAMPP, DisplayVersion 5.6.11-1, Publisher Bitnami, InstallDate 1440366248 and InstallLocation C:\xampp; the XAMPP directory and binaries have earlier timestamps matching vendor files.

value: The attacker host 192.168.56.102 used sqlmap against the web app, issuing command-execution probes through /tmpbiwuc.php and deleting the temporary files afterward.
evidence: grep 'tmpbiwuc.php' work/extracted/s50bb00/web/xampp/apache/logs/access.log; lines with 02/Sep/2015:04:25:53 -0700, 04:26:04 -0700 and 04:26:23 -0700.

value: The attacker browsed DVWA's upload module and posted a payload that became /dvwa/hackable/uploads/phpshell.php, then executed directory listing and commands through that webshell.
evidence: grep 'phpshell.php' work/extracted/s50bb00/web/xampp/apache/logs/access.log; lines with 03/Sep/2015:00:10:15 -0700, 00:15:58 -0700, 00:16:13 -0700, 00:17:58 -0700, 00:31:54 -0700.

value: The archive contains attacker webshell leftovers at /xampp/htdocs/DVWA/c99.php, /xampp/htdocs/DVWA/webshell.php, /xampp/htdocs/DVWA/webshells.zip, /xampp/htdocs/DVWA/hackable/uploads/phpshell.php, and /xampp/htdocs/DVWA/hackable/uploads/phpshell2.php.
evidence: sha256 / content inspection of extracted files; e.g. 'system($_GET["cmd"]);' in webshell.php and a reverse-shell target 192.168.56.102:4545 in phpshell2.php.

value: The observed intrusion is web-app exploitation with SQLMap-assisted command execution followed by DVWA file upload abuse and dropped PHP webshells.
evidence: Correlation of access.log entries for /tmpbiwuc.php, /dvwa/vulnerabilities/upload/, /dvwa/hackable/uploads/phpshell.php, and the extracted webshell contents.

value: XAMPP 5.6.11-1 was installed on the machine before the intrusion window and recorded in the uninstall registry key under the C:\xampp path.
evidence: regipy query of \\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Uninstall\\xampp shows InstallDate=1440366248, DisplayVersion=5.6.11-1, InstallLocation=C:\\xampp.

value: The attacker created an empty staging directory named abc under /dvwa/hackable/uploads via the uploaded PHP shell.
evidence: grep 'mkdir%20abc' work/extracted/s50bb00/logs/access.log; line 03/Sep/2015:00:17:58 -0700. Directory metadata for xampp/htdocs/DVWA/hackable/uploads/abc shows crtime 2015-09-03T07:17:58Z.

value: The attacker dropped a PHP reverse shell in /xampp/htdocs/DVWA/hackable/uploads/phpshell2.php that hard-codes 192.168.56.102:4545 as its callback target.
evidence: read the extracted file and note the hard-coded stream_socket_client('tcp://192.168.56.102:4545') connection string.

value: A five-byte file named data.txt containing 'hello' exists in the Administrator profile and was read through DVWA's file-inclusion bug.
evidence: open /Users/Administrator/data.txt in the image to read its contents; grep 'data.txt' work/extracted/s50bb00/logs/access.log to find the file-inclusion requests at 02/Sep/2015:02:33:23 -0700 and 02:36:48 -0700.

value: The attacker’s web activity follows a chained exploit path: DVWA login, SQL injection reconnaissance with sqlmap, local file inclusion, command execution, and PHP webshell upload/reuse.
evidence: lines 3943-3993 and 3853-4038 in access.log show /dvwa/vulnerabilities/fi/, /dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/, sqlmap user-agent strings, and the later /dvwa/vulnerabilities/upload/ and /dvwa/c99.php webshell requests.

value: The host's system time was reset during boot, marking the start of the captured activity window.
evidence: EventID 1 (Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-General); TimeCreated=2015-08-23 10:29:50.088999+00:00; parsed from work/extracted/s50bb01/System.evtx with python-evtx.

value: The host obtained DHCP lease parameters including 10.10.10.22 during startup.
evidence: EventID 1002 (Microsoft-Windows-Dhcp-Client); parsed from work/extracted/s50bb01/System.evtx with python-evtx; event data included 192.168.56.101, 080027A91613, and 10.10.10.22.

value: A local logon session was created at the start of the 2015-08-24 activity burst.
evidence: EventID 4624 (Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing); TimeCreated=2015-08-24 06:51:38.437500+00:00; parsed from work/extracted/s50bb01/Security.evtx with python-evtx.

value: Administrator/SYSTEM logon and privilege-use activity started, including 4672 privileges such as SeDebugPrivilege.
evidence: EventIDs 4624, 4648, and 4672 (Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing); parsed from work/extracted/s50bb01/Security.evtx with python-evtx; 4672 PrivilegeList included SeDebugPrivilege and SeImpersonatePrivilege.

value: The memory dump contains Meterpreter stage code; the embedded core/stdapi strings and WinINet/URLMon APIs are most consistent with a staged Meterpreter reverse HTTPS payload.
evidence: grep -aob 'Meterpreter has' inputs/memdump.mem; grep -aob 'InternetGetCertByURL' inputs/memdump.mem; grep -aob 'HttpOpenRequestW' inputs/memdump.mem; strings inputs/memdump.mem showed core_uuid, stdapi_fs_file_expand_path, InternetOpenUrlW, InternetGetCertByURL, and related WinINet/URLMon APIs.

value: Installed volatility3 2.28.2 into work/.toolchain to enable memory-forensics attempts.
evidence: Command: work/.toolchain/bin/pip install volatility3; output reported 'Successfully installed pefile-2024.8.26 volatility3-2.28.2'.

value: The SAM hive contains two attacker-added local user accounts, hacker and user1, under SAM\Domains\Account\Users\Names, and their Names subkeys were last modified at about 2015-09-02 09:05 UTC.
evidence: Command: work/.toolchain/bin/python query of SAM Names subkeys; output showed 'hacker lastwrite 130856583253789850' and 'user1 lastwrite 130856583060196100', which convert to 2015-09-02T09:05:25Z and 2015-09-02T09:05:06Z.

value: SAM shows the two custom local accounts hacker and user1 with RID subkeys 000003ED and 000003EE.
evidence: Command: work/.toolchain/bin/python query of SAM Domains/Account/Users Names and Users keys; output included subkeys 'hacker' and 'user1' and user RID keys '000003ED' and '000003EE'.

value: The memory image contains Meterpreter stage strings, indicating the shellcode used was Meterpreter (PHP Meterpreter stage).
evidence: Command: strings -a inputs/memdump.mem | grep -i -C 2 'Meterpreter'; output included 'Evaling main meterpreter stage' and comments about Meterpreter using File.expand_path.

value: Installed analysis dependencies pytsk3 20260715, regipy 6.3.0, python-evtx 0.8.1, and volatility3 2.28.2 into work/.toolchain/venv for case analysis.
evidence: bash install command and package versions shown in stdout

value: The SAM hive shows two attacker-created local user accounts, hacker (RID 1006) and user1 (RID 1005); their SAM name keys were last written on 2015-09-02 09:05 UTC and they are members of the Users and Remote Desktop Users built-in groups, not Administrators.
evidence: SAM\Domains\Account\Users\Names\hacker and \SAM\Domains\Account\Users\Names\user1; group membership by alias blobs in \SAM\Domains\Builtin\Aliases\00000221 and \SAM\Domains\Builtin\Aliases\0000022B; regipy SAMParsePlugin output and alias RID scan

value: Administrator's UserAssist records show CompMgmtLauncher.exe was executed, which supports that the new local accounts were added through the Computer Management / Local Users and Groups GUI rather than by direct registry editing.
evidence: HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\UserAssist decoded with rot13; UEME_RUNPATH:C:\Windows\System32\CompMgmtLauncher.exe

value: XAMPP 5.6.11-1 was installed at C:\xampp, with an InstallDate of 2015-08-23 and the desktop installer xampp-win32-5.6.11-1-VC11-installer.exe still present in Administrator's Desktop, indicating the web stack was explicitly installed on the box and not merely a stock Windows component.
evidence: HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\xampp values DisplayName= XAMPP, InstallLocation=C:\xampp, InstallDate=1440366248; /Users/Administrator/Desktop/xampp-win32-5.6.11-1-VC11-installer.exe timestamps

value: /Users/Administrator/Desktop/xampp-win32-5.6.11-1-VC11-installer.exe and C:\xampp are evidence of a third-party XAMPP web stack on the host.
evidence: UserAssist UEME_RUNPATH for the installer; HKLM uninstall key DisplayName/InstallLocation

value: Local accounts hacker (RID 1006) and user1 (RID 1005) were added to the box.
evidence: \SAM\Domains\Account\Users\Names\hacker and \SAM\Domains\Account\Users\Names\user1; SAMParsePlugin output; alias membership scan of 00000221 and 0000022B

value: XAMPP 5.6.11-1 at C:\xampp, with xampp-win32-5.6.11-1-VC11-installer.exe on the Administrator desktop, is a key software artifact on the host.
evidence: HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\xampp and UserAssist UEME_RUNPATH entries

value: XAMPP appears to predate the attacker-created accounts: its uninstall entry shows InstallDate 2015-08-23, whereas the attacker local accounts were created on 2015-09-02; this makes XAMPP look like preexisting victim software rather than a post-compromise implant.
evidence: HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\xampp InstallDate=1440366248 and SAM names last-write times for hacker/user1

value: Oracle VM VirtualBox Guest Additions 4.3.30 is present in the uninstall registry and VBoxTray autostart, which is consistent with the box being a virtual machine guest and not with an attacker dropper.
evidence: HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\Oracle VM VirtualBox Guest Additions 4.3.30 and HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\VBoxTray

value: Apache access logs show the attacker creating the `abc` directory via `GET /dvwa/hackable/uploads/phpshell.php?cmd=mkdir%20abc`, corroborating the bonus attacker-added `abc` directory entry.
evidence: line 7685 in access.log; verify with `grep -n 'mkdir%20abc' work/extracted/s50bb03/logs/access.log`

value: The captured memory is Meterpreter-based: the dump contains the main Meterpreter stage and standard stdapi/core strings, plus WinINet/URLMon HTTP(S) client APIs, which matches a staged reverse-HTTPS Meterpreter payload.
evidence: Verified with `grep -aob 'Meterpreter has' inputs/memdump.mem`, `grep -aob 'Evaling main meterpreter stage' inputs/memdump.mem`, and nearby strings showing core_uuid/stdapi_fs_file_expand_path, InternetOpenW/HttpOpenRequestW/HttpSendRequestW/InternetGetCertByURL and urlmon.dll / WININET.dll references.
